The actual depth of beaker in $mm$ is (when zero of vernier coincides with zero of main scale),
questions.solution:
We are measuring the depth from metallic strip of vernier calipers.

Given,

The least count of vernier calipers& $LS = 0 . 1mm = 0 . 01cm$

Main scale reading~$MSR = 6 . 4cm$

Vernier scale reading~$VSR = 4$

So the reading of the depth,$D = MSR + ( VSR \times LC ) = 6 . 4 + ( 4 \times 0 . 01 ) = 6 . 44cm$

Because, there is no zero error, so depth will be same as above.

The jaws of a vernier calipers touch the inner wall of calorimeter without any undue pressure. The position of zero of vernier scale on the main scale reads 3.48. The ${6}^{th }$of vernier scale division is coinciding with any main scale division. Vernier constant of calipers is $0 . 01cm .$ Find actual internal diameter of calorimeter, when it is observed that the vernier scale has a zero error of~$- 0 . 03cm$.
&
questions.solution:
The jaws of a vernier calipers& touch the inner wall means we are measuring inner radius.

Given,

The main scale reading& $MSR = 3 . 48cm$

The Least count of vernier calipers~$LC = 0 . 01cm$

The vernier scale reading~$VSR = 6$

Diameter of the calorimeter measured is,~

$D = MSR + \left(VSR \timesLC\right)$

$D = 3 . 48 + \left(0 . 01 \times6\right) = 3 . 54cm$

There is a negative zero error of~$- 0 . 03cm$. So, the actual diameter of the calorimeter will be,~

$D^{'} = D - zeroerror = 3 . 54 - \left(-0 . 03\right) = 3 . 57cm

$

questions.q: The length of an object is measured using a vernier system whose main scale is $30$ cm long with $600$ divisions. If $19$ divisions of the main scale coincide with $20$ divisions of the vernier scale, then its least count is
questions.solution:
$∵$ Least count $= MSD - VSD$

$∵ MSD = \left(\dfrac{30}{100}\right)600 = 5 \times {10}^{- 4}m$

and $VSD = \dfrac{19}{20} \times MSD$

$= \dfrac{19}{20} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4} = 4 .75 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$∴$ Least count $= \left(5 - 4 .75\right) \times {10}^{- 4} = 0 .025 mm$

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, resistances are connected as shown in figure. The balancing length ${l}_{1} = 55 cm$ . Now, an unknown resistance $x$ is connected in series with $P$ and the new balancing length is found to be $75cm$ . What is the value of The value of $11x$ (in ohm)?(Given, $P = 4Ω$ )
questions.solution:
Given in the meter bridge,

In $I$ st case, $\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{Q} = \dfrac{55}{100 - 55}$

$⇒ Q = \dfrac{4 \times 45}{55}$ ...(i)

In $2$ nd case, $\dfrac{P + x}{Q} = \dfrac{75}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4 + x}{3} = Q$ ...(ii)

From Equations (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{4 + x}{3} = \dfrac{36}{11}$

$4 + x = \dfrac{108}{11}$

$x = \dfrac{108 - 44}{11}$

$= \dfrac{64}{11}$

$⇒ 11x = 64$

questions.q: A student measures the distance covered and time taken by a body under free fall which was initially at rest. He uses this data for estimating $g$, the acceleration due to gravity. If the maximum percentage errors in measurement of the distance and the time are ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2}$ respectively, then the maximum possible percentage error in the estimation of $g$ is
questions.solution:
From the relation

$\text{h} = \text{ut} + \dfrac{1}{2} {gt}^{2}$

$\text{h} = \dfrac{1}{2} {gt}^{2} ⇒ \text{g} = \dfrac{2 \text{h}}{t^{2}} \left($∵ $\text{body initially at rest}\right)

Taking natural logarithms on both sides, we get

$ln \left(g\right) = ln \left(h\right) - 2ln\left(t\right) + ln\left(2\right)$

$\text{Differentiating,} $\dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{\text{g}} = \dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{\text{h}} -$2 $\dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{\text{t}}

For maximum permissible errors, we add both the errors. So

\left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{g} \times$100\$right)\text\max = \$left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{h} \times \text{100}\right) +2 $\times $\$left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{t} \times \text{100}\right)

\dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{\text{h}} \times \text{100} = {e}_{1} \text{and} \dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{\text{t}} \times \text{100} = {e}_{2}

$\text{Therefore,} {\left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{\text{g}} \times \text{100}\right)}_\max = {e}_{1} +2 {e}_{2}$

questions.q: Two full turns of the circular scale of a screw gauge having $50$ divisions cover a distance of $1$ mm.~Further, it is found that the screw gauge has a zero error of $- 0 . 02mm$. While measuring the diameter of a thin wire, a student notes the main scale reading of $4$ mm and the number of circular scale divisions in line with the main scale as $37$. The diameter of the wire is,
questions.solution:
Distance cover in $1$ full turn will be~$\dfrac{1mm}{2} = 0 . 5mm$.

Least count of screw gauge,

$LC = \dfrac{Distancecoverin1fullturn}{numberofdivisionincircularscale} = \dfrac{0 . 5mm}{50} = 0 . 01mm$

Reading of the screw gauge,$R = mainscalereading + Circularscalereading \times LC$

$R = 4mm + 37 \times 0 . 01mm = 4 . 37mm$

Reading without zero error,~$R^{'} = R - zeroerror = 4 . 37mm - \left(- 0 . 02mm\right) = 4 . 39mm$

questions.q: In a Searle's experiment, the diameter of the wire as measured by a screw gauge is $0 . 050cm$. The pitch of screw gauge is $2mm$ and number of divisions on circular scale is $200$. The length, measured by a scale of least count $0 . 1cm$, is $100cm$. When a weight of $50N$ is suspended from the wire, the elongation is measured to be $0 . 125cm$ by a micrometer of least count $0 . 001cm$. Find the maximum percentage error in the measurement of Young's modulus of the material of the wire from these data. Round off answer to nearest integer
questions.solution:
First, recall the formula of Young's modulus in terms of force applied, cross- sectional area of the wire and strain produced,

$y = \dfrac{mg}{A}\dfrac{l}{\Deltal} = \dfrac{mg}{\pi{r}^{2}}\dfrac{l}{\Deltal}$,

So, the percentage error in Young's modulus,

$\dfrac{\Deltay}{y} \times 100 = \left[\dfrac{2\Deltar}{r} + \dfrac{\Deltal}{l} + \left[\Delta\dfrac{\left(\Deltal\right)}{\Deltal}\right]\right] \times 100$

$= \left[2 \times \dfrac{0 . 001}{0 . 05} + \dfrac{0 . 1}{100} + \dfrac{0 . 001}{0 . 125}\right] \times 100$

$= \left[\dfrac{2}{50} + \dfrac{1}{1000} + \dfrac{1}{125}\right] \times 100$

$= \left[0 . 04 + 0 . 001 + 0 . 008\right] \times 100 = 4 . 90$.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $25Ω$ is connected to a battery of $2V$ along with a resistance of $3000Ω$. In this case, a full-scale deflection of $30units$ is obtained in the galvanometer. In order to reduce this deflection to $10units$, how much more resistance (in $Ω$) should be added to the circuit in series?
questions.solution:
The deflection in a galvanometer is directly proportional to the current.

First case:

$30x = \dfrac{2}{25 + 3000}$

Second case:

$10x = \dfrac{2}{25 + 3000 + R}$

$⇒ 3 = \dfrac{25 + 3000 + R}{25 + 3000}$

On solving, we get

$R = 6050Ω$

A screw gauge having $50$ divisions in the circular scale and pitch as $1$ mm.
questions.solution:
As per the given data the vernier has a least count of $0 . 01cm$, which is consistent with the information given in the question.

The measured value of the length of the rod$= 3 . 50cm$

So, the least count of the measuring instrument must be

$0 . 01cm = 0 . 1mm$

For the vernier scale

$10MSD = 1cm = 10mm$

$\to 1MSD = 1mm$

also $9MSD = 10VSD$

$∴$~Least count (L.C.)

$= 1MSD - 1VSD$

$= ( 1 - 0 . 9 ) mm$

$= 0 . 1mm$

questions.q: The main scale of a vernier caliper reads $10$ mm in $10$ divisions. $10$ divisions of vernier scale coincide with $9$ divisions of the main scale. When the two jaws of the calipers touch each other, the fifth division of the vernier coincides with a~main scale division and the zero of the vernier is to the right of zero of the main scale. When a cylinder is tightly placed between the two jaws, the zero of vernier scale lies slightly to the left of $3.2$ cm& and the fourth vernier division coincides with the main scale division. The diameter of the cylinder is,
questions.solution:
$LC = \dfrac{1}{10}mm = 0 . 01cm$

and~$e = VSD \times LC = 0 . 05cm$

Therefore,

$TSR = MSR + ( VSD \times LC ) - e$

$⇒ TSR = 3 . 1 + ( 4 \times 0 . 01 ) - 0 . 05$

$⇒ TSR = 3 . 14 - 0 . 05 = 3 . 09cm$

If the first and the second resonance are measured at ${l ⁡}_{1} = 2 4.0 cm$ and ${l ⁡}_{2} = \text{74.70} cm$, then the permissible error in speed of sound is

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $50Ω$ is connected to a battery of $3V$ along with a resistance of $2950Ω$ in series. A full-scale deflection of $30$ divisions is obtained in the galvanometer. In order to reduce this deflection to $20$ divisions, the resistance in series should be
questions.solution:
Current through the galvanometer

$I = \dfrac{3}{( 50 + 2950 )} = {10}^{- 3}\text{A}$

Current for 30 divisions $= {10}^{- 3}\text{A}$

Current for 20 divisions

$= \dfrac{{10}^{- 3}}{30} \times 20 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times {10}^{- 3}\text{A}$



For the same deflection to obtain for 20 divisions, let resistance added be R

$∴ \dfrac{2}{3} \times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{3}{\left(50 + R\right)}$

$orR = 4450Ω$

questions.q: The length of a magnet is large compared to its width and breadth. The time period of its oscillation in a vibration magnetometer is $2s$. The magnent is cut into three equal parts of length $\dfrac{L}{3}$ each,and three parts are then placed on each other with their like poles together. The time period of this combination will be
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillations of magnet

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{ \left(\dfrac{I}{M{B}_{H}}\right)} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Where $I =$ moment of inertia of magnet

$= $\dfrac{mL^{2}}{12} (m, being the mass of magnet)

Now magnet is cut into three equal parts.

When the three equal parts of magnet are placed on one another with their like poles together, then

$I^{′} = $\dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{m}{3}\right) \times {\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)}^{2} \times$3$

$= $\dfrac{1}{12}\dfrac{mL^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{I}{9}

and $M^{′} =$ pole strength $\times $\dfrac{L}{3} \times$3 = M$

Hence,

$⇒ T^{′} = $\dfrac{1}{3} \timesT

$T^{′} = $\dfrac{2}{3}$s$
